candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0102.

options.A: Reassure the client that infection symptoms are expected during early clozapine therapy and can be reviewed at the next scheduled psychiatric visit.
options.B: Arrange prompt clinical evaluation and an ANC because infection symptoms can signal clozapine-associated neutropenia, which remains a serious risk.
options.C: Tell the client to stop all laboratory monitoring because the federal clozapine REMS program was removed and blood counts are no longer useful.
options.D: Advise the client to continue clozapine unchanged for several days and seek evaluation only if a widespread rash or facial swelling develops.

candidate.rationale: FDA removed the clozapine REMS in 2025, but the risk of severe neutropenia remains. Current FDA guidance and prescribing information continue to support ANC monitoring, and infection symptoms such as fever, chills, or sore throat require prompt medical evaluation rather than routine follow-up.
candidate.source_claim_supported: REMS removed effective June 13, 2025; severe neutropenia risk remains and ANC monitoring continues under prescribing information.
candidate.source_document_title: Clozapine REMS Removal and Neutropenia Safety Communication
candidate.source_locator: FDA Drug Safety Communication — REMS removal effective June 13, 2025; section for health care professionals on severe neutropenia and ANC monitoring
candidate.source_version_date: FDA communication current as of 2026-08-16; REMS removed effective 2025-06-13
candidate.stem: A client taking clozapine for 6 weeks calls the clinic with fever, chills, and a new sore throat. Which nursing response best reflects current FDA safety guidance?
